*Session Title: The Reality of Sufism-Dealing with Legacy of the Righteous
Description: بين حقيقة التصوّف وأفعال بعض المتصوّفة. نظرة عامة على الحكم العطائية وكيف نتعامل مع أقوال الصالحين“Between the true essence of Sufism and the actions of some Sufis:An overview of the Hikam of Ibn ʿAṭā’ Allāh and how we should approach the sayings of the righteous.” In the vast landscape of Islamic spirituality, Sufism represents the inward dimension of faith— the pursuit of Ihsan and the refinement of the heart. Yet its path is often misunderstood, suspended between the noble ideals of its early tradition and the problematic practices that later appeared in some circles.This session offers a calm, balanced, and practical exploration of that tension. We will clarify the authentic essence of Tasawwuf, grounded firmly in the Qur’an and Sunnah, and distinguish it from the blameworthy innovations that must be avoided.This year’s theme brings a unique opportunity as we delve into selected wisdoms from the renowned sage Ibn ʿAṭā’ Allāh. Some of you may know his sayings well, while others may wonder: Why study the reflections of this scholar? Why not limit ourselves to the sayings of the Prophet ﷺ, or the teachings of the Companions? And more broadly, how should we approach the words of our righteous predecessors—whether Ibn ʿAṭā’ Allāh, Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn al-Qayyim, Imam Aḥmad, or even a beloved teacher who has passed on?This introductory session aims to establish the right mindset: understanding how their lives and insights can inspire spiritual growth while remembering that they are not sources of law.In the sessions ahead, we will examine one wisdom from Ibn ʿAṭā’ Allāh at a time—using each as a lens to recalibrate our thinking and transform our daily practice.

*Session Title: The Unplanted Seed - Bury Your Ego and Grow
Description: "إدفن وجودك في أرض الخمول فما نبت مما لم يدفن لا يتم نتاجه" “Bury your existence in the earth of obscurity, for whatever sprouts forth, without having first been buried, flowers imperfectly.” In a culture driven by visibility, recognition, and instant validation, this teaching invites us to embrace hiddenness, humility, and sincere inner work. Imam Ibn ʿAṭā’ Allāh reminds us that just as a seed must be buried before it can grow, our spiritual growth demands periods of obscurity—moments where our deeds, struggles, and efforts remain unseen except by Allah. This session will unpack what it means to cultivate sincerity, to grow away from the spotlight, and to allow Allah—not people—to develop our character and elevate our rank.

*Session Title: From Fog to Light - Purifying the Heart for Divine Connection
Description: "كيف يشرق قلب صور الأكوان منطبعة في مرآته؟ أم كيف يرحل إلى الله، وهو مكبل بشهواته؟ أم كيف يطمع أن يدخل حضرة ألله، وهو لم يتطهر من جنابة غفلاته؟ أم كيف يرجو أن يفهم دقائق الأسرار، وهو لم يتب من هفواته؟" "How can your heart shine with fog imprinted on its mirror? How can it journey to God while shackled by its desires? How can it hope to enter God's presence while it has not purified itself from the impurity of its negligence? How can it hope to understand the subtleties of secrets while it has not repented from its lapses?" In this session, we reflect on one of Imam Ibn ʿAṭā’ Allāh’s most direct and soul-awakening wisdoms. Through a series of probing rhetorical questions—“How can your heart shine…?” “How can it journey…?”—he confronts the spiritual barriers that prevent a believer from drawing near to Allah. These lines challenge us to examine the internal “rust” that dims our hearts, the desires that restrain our spiritual journey, the negligence that blocks us from divine closeness, and the sins from which we have yet to repent. This wisdom is not meant to condemn, but to awaken: to push us toward cleansing, discipline, self-awareness, and sincere tawbah as the necessary foundations for spiritual illumination.

*Session Title: The Company You Keep - How Friends Shape Your Faith
Description: "لا تصحب من لا ينهضك حاله، ولا يدلك على الله مقاله" “Do not befriend someone whose character does not uplift you, nor whose words do not guide you to God.” This wisdom teaches that friends are not just social company—they are spiritual influences who either elevate us or pull us down. Our hearts are shaped by the people we allow closest to us. Imam Ibn ʿAṭā’ Allāh calls us to choose companions who strengthen our character, remind us of Allah, and help us grow—not those who distract, drain, or derail us. This session highlights the criteria of beneficial friendship, the dangers of spiritually empty companionship, and practical steps to cultivate relationships that nourish faith.

*Session Title: "I'll Do It When I'm Free" – The Ultimate Deception
Description: "إحالتك الأعمال على وجود الفراغ - من رعونات النفس" “The sign of a reckless soul is one that delays good deeds thinking it has free time.” This wisdom confronts a universal human weakness—procrastination in worship, delayed repentance, postponing growth, and assuming we have endless tomorrows. Ibn ʿAṭā’ Allāh calls this delay not just laziness, but recklessness, because it denies the fragility of life and the urgency of the spiritual path. This session explores why the soul delays good, how false assumptions about “future time” weaken our faith, and practical ways to break the cycle of postponement and step into immediate action.

*Session Title: The Root of All Good - A Lesson in Spiritual Dissatisfaction
Description: "أصل كل معصية وغفلة وشهوة الرضا عن النفس، وأصل كل طاعة ويقظة وعفة عدم الرضى عنها"The root of all sin, negligence, and lust is self-satisfaction. The root of all obedience, vigilance, and chastity is dissatisfaction with oneself. Through this wisdom, Ibn ʿAṭā’ Allāh teaches us that spiritual downfall does not begin with a major sin—it begins with a subtle inner attitude: being pleased with oneself. When a person becomes overly impressed with their own deeds, excuses their own faults, or stops seeing the need to grow, the heart opens the door to laziness, desires, and disobedience. On the other hand, a believer who remains humble, self-aware, and inwardly dissatisfied with their flaws is protected from arrogance and motivated toward constant improvement. This session explores how self-satisfaction blinds the heart, how healthy self-critique fuels spiritual excellence, and how to cultivate humility that leads to closeness with Allah.

*Session Title: Panel Discussion [The Intimacy of Isolation - Finding Allah in Loneliness and Prayer]

*Session Title: The Great Paradox - Chasing Illusions, Fleeing Reality
Description: "العجب كل العجب من من يهرب مما لا انفكاك له عنه، ويطلب ما لا بقاء له معه، فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار ولكن تعمى القلوب التي في الصدور" It is truly astonishing that someone would flee from what they cannot escape, and seek what they cannot remain with. For it is not the eyes that are blind, but the hearts within the chests. In this profound saying, Imam Ibn Aṭā’ Allāh exposes one of humanity’s deepest contradictions: our tendency to run from what is unavoidable—death, accountability, destiny—while chasing after what is fleeting and cannot stay with us—dunya, people, wealth, status, and moments of pleasure. At its core, this Hikmah reminds us that true blindness is not the inability to see with the eyes, but the inability to perceive truth with the heart. This session reflects on how spiritual blindness develops, how we often miscalculate what is worth pursuing, and how to realign our hearts with what is eternal, stable, and meaningful.

*Session Title: Let Go and Let God - The Art of Spiritual Trust

We often expend our energy pursuing what is fleeting or certain—wealth, status, comfort—while neglecting what truly matters for our soul: obedience, accountability, and preparation for the Hereafter. *Session Title: Divine Denial - When 'No' is a Gift
Description: ربّما أعطاك فمنعك وربّما منعك فأعطاك ومتى فتح لك باب الفهم في المنع صار المنع عين العطاء .كتاب إيقاظ الهمم في شرح الحكمPerhaps He gave you and then withheld, and perhaps He withheld from you and then gave you. And when He opens for you the door of understanding in withholding, then withholding itself becomes a form of giving. This saying challenges our limited perspective on life’s trials and apparent losses. What we perceive as deprivation may actually be a blessing in disguise, and what we receive may require careful stewardship. The key lies in understanding: when the heart grasps the wisdom behind Allah’s actions, even what seems like “withholding” can be experienced as a form of divine giving—spiritual growth, patience, insight, and closeness to Allah. This session explores patience, trust in divine wisdom, and transforming perception of hardship into gratitude and spiritual gain.

*Session Title: From Shock to Solace in a World of Sorrows
Description: “لاتستغرب وقوع الأكدار، مادامت في هذه الدار، فإنها ما أبرزت إلا ماهو مستحَقُّ وصفها وواجب نعته”“Do not be astonished by the occurrence of calamities, as long as you remain in this world, for it only manifests what is deserving of its description and appropriate to be attributed to it.” This wisdom reminds us that suffering, hardship, and misfortune are intrinsic to worldly life. They are neither random nor unjust; they reveal the reality of human existence, test our hearts, and expose what is naturally due in this transient world. Understanding this allows a believer to approach calamities with patience, acceptance, and spiritual insight, rather than surprise or despair.

*Session Title: The Deception of Deeds - When Obedience Isn't Enough
Description: “ربما فتح لك باب الطاعة و ما يفتح لك باب القبول، و ربما قضى عليك الذنب فكان سببا في الوصول، فمعصية أورثت ذلا و افتقارا خير من طاعة أورثت عزا واستكبارا" “Sometimes He opens the door of obedience for you, but not the door of acceptance; or sometimes He condemns you to sin, and it turns out to be a cause for union with God. *Session Title: Raising Men and Women, Not Kids
Description: In an age of hyper-protection, distraction, and identity confusion, many children grow up shielded from struggle but also disconnected from their purpose. Yet our Islamic tradition presents a radically different model: youth who carried revelation, defended the Prophet ﷺ, preserved the Qur’an, led armies, resolved disputes, and shaped the future of this Ummah. This two-part session explores how to raise resilient, confident, spiritually grounded children in today’s world. Through Prophetic guidance, examples from early Muslim youth, and practical strategies for modern families, we will examine how to nurture children who are not just practicing Muslims—but ambassadors of Islam, builders of community, and inheritors of a legacy that outlives us. Together, we will dive into how to cultivate identity, instill responsibility, and develop faith-centered habits that become generational Sadaqah jariyah.

*Session Title: تجاهات الصراع في اليمن والتأثيرات الإقليمية والدولية في تحديد تلك الإتجاها
Description: تتناول هذه الجلسة قراءة معمّقة للمشهد اليمني الراهن، في تقاطعه بين التوازنات الإقليمية والتحولات الداخلية. فعلى الصعيد الدولي، يقف الملف اليمني عند مفترق حساس تتداخل فيه الاستراتيجية العالمية مع أولويات دول الخليج من جهة، ومع معادلات المواجهة غير المباشرة مع إيران من جهة أخرى، مما يجعل اليمن ساحة مركزية لإعادة رسم خرائط النفوذ الإقليمي.أما داخلياً، فسنستعرض أبرز التطورات الإنسانية والحقوقية التي يعيشها الشعب اليمني في ظل سنوات طويلة من الحرب والانقسام، مع تسليط الضوء على التحديات المعيشية، وحالة المؤسسات، ووضع النازحين، والملامح العامة للمشهد الحقوقي.كما ستتناول الجلسة أهم العوائق التي ما زالت تمنع إخراج الملف اليمني من “عنق الزجاجة”، سواء كانت سياسية، عسكرية، إقليمية، أو مرتبطة بالمشهد الاقتصادي والأمني داخل البلد.تهدف الجلسة إلى تقديم فهم شامل يساعد الحضور على استيعاب الواقع الحالي، وقراءة مساراته المستقبلية، واستشراف السيناريوهات المحتملة لإعادة بناء الدولة وتحقيق الأمن والاستقرار.
Description_English: This session deals with an in-depth reading of the current Yemeni landscape, intersection of regional and internal adjustments. At the international level, the Yemeni file is at a delicate crossroads in which the global strategy overlaps with the priorities of the Gulf States on the one hand, and the indirect confrontational equivalence with Iran on the other, thus making Yemen a central arena for reshaping regional influence maps. Internally, we will review the most notable humanitarian and legal developments of the Yemeni people in long years of war and division, highlighting the challenges of living, the situation of institutions, the status of displaced persons and the general features of the legal landscape. The session will also address the main obstacles that continue to prevent the removal of the Yemeni file from the " glass neck " , whether political, military, regional or linked to the economic and security landscape within the country. The aim of the meeting is to provide a comprehensive understanding that will help the audience to understand current realities, to read their future paths and to explore possible scenarios for rebuilding the State and to achieve security and stability.

*Session Title: Jannah Seekers, Active Hunters
Description: The famous statement of the Prophet ﷺ — “‘Ukāsha has beaten you to it” — captures a timeless truth about the path to Jannah: Paradise is for those who seize opportunities, not those who wait for them.When the Prophet ﷺ mentioned that seventy thousand from his Ummah would enter Jannah without accountability, ‘Ukāsha ibn Muḥsin immediately stood up and requested, “O Messenger of Allah, ask Allah to make me one of them.” His readiness, clarity, and spiritual ambition earned him the prophetic affirmation: “You are one of them.”A second man asked for the same privilege — but the Prophet ﷺ responded, “Ukāsha beat you to it.” Not because the door was closed, but because a high standard had been set: Jannah belongs to the active seekers, the spiritually ambitious, the ones who hunt opportunities instead of hesitating.“Jannah Seeker… Active Hunter” reminds us that Paradise is not for the passive, the indecisive, or the occasionally inspired. It is for those whose hearts are alive —those who pray with purpose, strive with discipline, repent quickly, serve consistently, and carry a mindset shaped by eternal outcomes.In this session, two speakers will guide us through what it truly means to actively pursue Jannah — with intentionality, consistency, and sincere effort. Together, they will explore the spiritual psychology, practical habits, and mindset transformations needed for every believer to become an “active hunter” of Allah’s pleasure and reward.

Using the Quran and Sunnah Effectively in Dawah Conversations
Description: The Qur’an and Sunnah are the foundation of all da‘wah. Yet, many da‘ees struggle to use them effectively—either quoting texts without context, sounding overly academic, or relying on personal opinions instead of revelation. In an age of skepticism, misinformation, and emotional sensitivity, the art of bringing Allah’s words and the Prophet’s teachings into a conversation requires wisdom, emotional intelligence, and strategic guidance.This training explores how to anchor da‘wah in revelation without overwhelming the listener, how to select the right ayat and hadith for the right moment, how to speak from the tradition with humility, and how to use the prophetic method of gradual teaching, persuasion, and compassion. Participants will learn practical strategies to make Qur’anic wisdom relatable, conversational, and deeply impactful for the people they speak to.By the end of the session, da‘ees will feel more confident quoting texts accurately, contextualizing them properly, and using them in a way that touches hearts rather than winning arguments.

*Session Title: Unleashing the Power of Tawwakul
Only God Can Judge Me
Description: For many of us, we first heard the phrase “only God can judge me” in college, but is it appropriate to use that as an excuse to justify our actions? We live in a time of hair reveals when taking off the hijab, posting videos of us smoking and partying, flaunting of haram relationships, etc. We are broadcasting our sins hiding behind the idea that only God can judge. College is a time of self-discovery, but what happens if it results in us disconnecting from Islam altogether? The Prophet PBUH advised us of the harm in exposing our sins: "All my Ummah will be forgiven except those who expose their sins. Among them is a man who commits a sin at night, and though Allah conceals it, in the morning he says, ‘I did such-and-such last night’ – while Allah had kept it hidden. He spent the night under the cover of his Lord, and in the morning he tore away Allah's cover from himself” (Sahih Bukhari). How can we protect ourselves from exposing our own sins? Is it true that only Allah SWT can judge me?

We'll stand with centuries-old and historical models where this fact has been manifested, learn how to live with certainty in the midst of trouble, and how to stay firm when the Earth shatters around us.

*Session Title: Panel Discussion Muslim Moms: Choosing Patience in the Hardest Moments
Description: Motherhood is a sacred calling—one honored in the Qur’an, elevated by the Prophet ﷺ, and essential to the health and future of our Ummah. Yet for many Muslim mothers today, the reality is heavy: emotional burnout, social isolation, rising expectations, and endless demands at home, work, and community.This session brings together two Muslim mothers—grounded in faith, experience, and practical wisdom along with profession in counseling —to have an honest conversation about the moments that push patience to its limits. From the toddler years to teenage challenges, from juggling work and home to navigating identity and spiritual growth, this discussion will explore what sabr truly looks like in real life.Together, the panelists will reflect on Prophetic examples, the emotional load mothers carry, and the spiritual tools our tradition offers. Attendees will gain realistic strategies for managing overwhelm, nurturing their own mental and spiritual well-being, and cultivating a home environment built on mercy, love, and intentionality.This is not a session about perfection—it’s about companionship on the journey, recognizing weaknesses without shame, and empowering mothers with faith-driven resilience.

*Session Title: Voices of South Asia: Justice, Rights, and the Future of Pakistan, Bangladesh & Kashmir
Description: This session provides a comprehensive and timely overview of three pivotal regions in South Asia—Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Kashmir—each navigating its own complex intersection of politics, identity, and justice. We will explore Pakistan’s renewed emphasis on Islamic solidarity, its internal political fluctuations, and the social pressures shaping its role within the wider Muslim world. Shifting priorities, economic challenges, and geopolitical alliances continue to influence how the country positions itself on key Ummah-related issues. In contrast, Bangladesh’s evolving nationalist identity presents another trajectory—one where historical memory, economic development, cultural pride, and political consolidation intersect. As the state continues to redefine what it means to be Bangladeshi, we will examine how these shifts impact democratic space, minority rights, and the region’s long-term stability. Finally, we turn to Kashmir, where an unresolved and decades-long struggle for self-determination remains one of the most sensitive and enduring crises in the Muslim world. Despite global attention waxing and waning, the humanitarian, political, and demographic realities on the ground continue to evolve with profound implications for justice and human rights. Together, these updates highlight the region’s broader themes: Who gets to define national identity? Whose rights are protected—or suppressed? And how do global and regional powers shape the future of millions? This talk aims to provide clarity, context, and a deeper understanding of the socioeconomic and political dynamics at play—helping attendees grasp both the challenges and the opportunities for meaningful advocacy and engagement.

*Session Title: للرجال فقط دور الأب في بناء شخصية الابن وطمأنينة الابنة
Description: في زمن تتسارع فيه التحديات التربوية وتزداد فيه الضغوط الاجتماعية والنفسية على الأبناء، يبرز دور الأب كركيزة أساسية في استقرار الأسرة وتوازنها. هذه الجلسة الخاصة بالرجال تسلط الضوء على التأثير العميق للأب في تشكيل شخصية الابن، وبناء ثقته، وتوجيه طاقته، كما تتناول الدور الحساس للأب في منح الابنة الشعور بالأمان، والقيمة، والاحتواء.الحديث ليس عن الأب الغائب أو القاسي، بل عن الأب الحاضر الواعي الذي يفهم أن القيادة ليست سلطة، بل مسؤولية، وأن الحزم لا يتعارض مع الرحمة، وأن حضوره العاطفي يترك أثرًا لا يمحوه الزمن.جلسة صادقة وعميقة للآباء، ومن سيصبحون آباء، لإعادة تعريف معنى الأبوة في ضوء القرآن والسنة والتجربة الواقعية.

This men ' s session highlights the profound influence of the father in shaping the son ' s personality, building his trust and guiding his capacity, as well as the sensitive role of the father in giving the daughter a feeling of safety, value and containment. A sincere and deep meeting of parents, who will be fathers, to redefine the meaning of parenthood in the light of the Koran, the Year and the real experience.

*Session Title: للنساء فقط قلوب ثابتة رغم العواصف - نساء ربّانيات في كل زمن
Description: في زمن تتكاثر فيه الضغوط، وتزداد فيه الفتن، وتُربَك فيه الهُويات، تبقى المرأة المسلمة مطالبة أن تكون ثابتة في قلب العاصفة، لا منكسرة ولا ضائعة، بل راسخة الجذور، ممتدة الروح، حيّة الإيمان. قلب المرأة اليوم يتعرض لرياح كثيرة: خوف على الأبناء، ضغوط المجتمع، صراع الأدوار، مقارنة مستمرة، وموجات من الشك والإرهاق. ومع ذلك، فإن التاريخ الإسلامي يخبرنا أن أعظم القلوب ثباتًا في المحن كانت قلوب النساء: أمهات، وزوجات، ومربيات، ومجاهدات بالصبر والإيمان.هذه المحاضرة ليست عن المثالية… بل عن الواقعية المؤمنة. ليست عن نساء خارقات… بل عن نساء ربانيات: يعرفن الله، فيثبتن عند البلاء، ويزهرن في زمن القحط، ويصبحن نورًا لغيرهن وهن في قلب الألم. سنتحدث عن الثبات… لا كقوة جامدة، بل كطمأنينة حية، وعن الربانية… لا كشعارات، بل كحياة يومية مليئة بالإيمان والوعي واليقين.
Description_English: In a time when pressures are growing, there is an increase in fatigue, and in which identities are raised, Muslim women remain required to be fixed in the heart of the storm, neither broken nor lost, but rooted, long-spirited, alive. Women ' s heart today is exposed to many winds: fear for children, pressure from society, conflict of roles, constant comparison, waves of doubt and exhaustion. However, Islamic history tells us that the greatest hearts in distress were women ' s hearts: mothers, wives, nurseries, patience and faith. This lecture isn't about idealism... but about honest reality. It's not about super-female women... but about Japanese women: they know God, they prove to purity, they blossom in time of degradation, and they become the light of others in the heart of pain. We'll talk about persistence... not as a force of rigidity, but as a living tranquillity, not as slogans, but as a daily life full of faith, consciousness and certainty.

*Session Title: Your Digital Footprint
Description: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ told us, “When a person dies, all their deeds end except three: a continuing charity, beneficial knowledge, and a child who prays for them.” But what happens to our social media? In our current times, social media is used for everything: our personal lives, our MSA, or masjid youth group. We know, however, that someone’s social media does not die with them. At a time when social media is used for flaunting materialism, how can we use it in a way that is pleasing to Allah SWT both within our lives and after our deaths?

*Session Title: Spousal & Parenting Balance
Description: Balancing marriage and parenting is one of the most challenging responsibilities of modern family life. Attendees will walk away with faith-centered tools to build balance, nurture the marital bond, and cultivate a home environment where parents and children thrive together.

*Session Title: Redefining Muslim Women Leadership
From Ta’if to Uhud to GAZA… Resilience in Chaotic Times
Description: Throughout the Seerah, the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) endured moments of intense pain, rejection, and trauma — yet responded with unwavering faith, emotional steadiness, and moral clarity. From the heartbreak of Ta’if, to the devastating losses at Uhud, to the suffocating siege of the Trench, his resilience became the foundation upon which the early Muslim community survived and later thrived.Today, Muslims — especially youth — face their own version of Ta’if and Uhud: stress, failures, public hostility, Islamophobia, family tension, academic pressure, and the overwhelming grief of witnessing the atrocities in Gaza and elsewhere in the Ummah.This session explores how the Prophetic model offers a roadmap for enduring pain with dignity, protecting the heart during hardship, and transforming struggle into spiritual and communal strength.This session will walk the audience through a sequential journey:Personal inner resilience — how the Prophet handled emotional wounds, rejection, setbacks, and pressure.Communal resilience — how we, as American Muslims, channel pain into purpose, solidarity, and long-term empowerment for the Ummah today.

*Session Title: The Arabian Gulf After Gaza: Power Shifts, Social Changes, and the Struggle for Justice
Description: The ongoing genocide in Gaza has triggered a profound recalibration across the Arabian Gulf—politically, socially, and ideologically. As global pressure mounts and regional rivalries sharpen, Gulf states are re-writing their strategies in real time: from accelerated normalization efforts with the Zionist entity to the bold social transformation campaigns to shifting human-rights boundaries.This talk provides a clear and timely overview of the latest developments in the Gulf region—Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Oman—and how each state is navigating the post-October-7 landscape. We will explore how Gaza is influencing state policies, public sentiment, internal reforms, and the broader regional balance of power.Participants will leave with an informed, nuanced understanding of: • The status and future of Gulf-Zionist normalization efforts • Human-rights implications and new internal security priorities • Social and cultural reforms and their ideological underpinnings • How the Gulf’s choices today shape the broader Muslim world tomorrowThis session equips audiences with the context needed to understand the rapidly evolving Gulf landscape—and why it matters deeply for the Ummah.

*Session Title: Unapologetically Muslim: Owning Our Narrative, Shaping Our Future
Description: In a time when Muslim identity is challenged from every direction—media narratives, political rhetoric, campus environments, and workplace pressures—many young Muslims feel overwhelmed, misunderstood, or hesitant to fully embrace who they are. This session calls us back to the heart of our strength: our affiliation with Islam, and our dedication to the deen.“Unapologetically Muslim” is an empowering session designed to help young Muslims reclaim confidence in their faith, tell their own story, and become proactive contributors to the present and future of the American Muslim community. Rather than reacting to external pressure, we learn how to shape our narrative, assert our values, and lead with clarity, courage, and pride.The talk will cover two essential phases of empowerment:Owning our narrative today—confronting Islamophobia, reframing identity, and navigating hostile or confusing environments with confidence and clarity.Shaping our future tomorrow—building leadership, vision, and long-term agency so the next generation becomes architects of the Ummah’s future—not spectators.With Islamic grounding, practical strategies, and a forward-looking approach, this session equips Muslims, especially the emerging younger generation, to step into society not as intimidated minorities, but as confident Muslims driven by purpose, values, and impact.

Description: في عالمٍ يزداد اضطرابًا وخوفًا وغموضًا، تأتي هذه الآية العظيمة من سورة الشعراء لتوقظ في القلوب يقينًا لا يتزعزع: أن الله معنا دائمًا، يرعانا، ويقودنا للطريق وإن بدا كل شيء مظلمًا.هذه الجلسة المزدوجة تسعى إلى إعادة بناء مفهوم اليقين بالله في زمن الفتن، الحروب، الظلم، فقدان الثبات، والضياع الداخلي.سيتناول المتحدثان كيف نحيا بهذا اليقين عمليًا: في الخوف، الفقد، القلق، الضغط الاجتماعي، والانكسار، وكيف نصنع من اليقين قوةً نفسية وروحية تُعين المسلم على الثبات، الطمأنينة، والوضوح في الطريق.
Description_English: In an increasingly turbulent, intimidating and ambiguous world, this great receptacle of poetry comes from an unwavering repression of hearts: God is always with us, caring for us, leading us to the road and if everything seems dark. Speakers will address how to live with this certainty in practice: in fear, loss, concern, social pressure, depression, and how to create certain psychological and spiritual power that will help Muslims to remain stable, reassuring and clear on the way.

*Session Title: From Gaza to the Quad
Description: The Student Intifada has been globalized throughout the past 2 years. The people of Gaza have told us repeatedly that they see and appreciate our efforts. Now, 26 months into what feels like a never-ending genocide, how can we maintain our unwavering support for the Palestinian people on our school campuses? From divestment to BDS campaigns, what are ways we can engage with our campus communities to fight towards the liberation of Palestine? How can we keep our torch lit despite feeling like our efforts are in vain?

*Session Title: Stories to Snapshot: Keeping Faith & Family Connected
Description: Between busy schedules, different languages, and grandkids who seem glued to their screens, many Muslim families wonder: How do we help our parents connect with our children without everyone ending up frustrated? And for grandparents, you're wondering, “ Why does my grandchild only respond to text messages?”This session brings elders and adult caregivers together to laugh a little, sigh in relief, and finally make sense of these cross-generational challenges. Drawing from the Qur’an, Sunnah, and heartwarming stories, we’ll explore simple, faith-rooted ways to strengthen the grandparent–grandchild bond, even in today’s fast-paced, Western world. If you’re looking for hope, practical ideas, and a reminder that your family is not alone, join us. There is a light at the end of the tunnel, and it’s brighter than you think.

*Session Title: The Ummah: Supported by People When Rulers Fail — Gaza & Sudan as Case Studies
Description: Across the globe, the suffering of Muslims in Gaza and Sudan has revealed a painful truth: when political leaders remain silent, complicit, or constrained, it is ordinary believers, civil society, and people of conscience who carry the weight of defending justice. From American Muslim organizations advocating relentlessly, to humanitarian workers risking everything on the ground, to voices within Turkish civil society and parliament pushing back against political inertia—real support for the Ummah has risen from the people, not the palaces.This panel brings together three distinct yet interconnected perspectives to explore how the global Muslim community responds when rulers fail to uphold moral responsibility. By examining Gaza and Sudan as case studies, we will analyze the gaps in governmental action, highlight the historic and spiritual legacy of people-led solidarity, and lay out practical models for transnational, community-driven support.Participants will gain a deeper understanding of how advocacy, relief work, and political courage can align to serve oppressed Muslims—and how the Ummah must continue building people-powered structures for justice, regardless of states’ shortcomings.

*Session Title: Emotional Intelligence for the Da'ees
Description: Delivering da‘wah is not only about what we say—it’s about how we say it, how we make people feel, and how we understand the emotional and mental landscape of those we speak to. The Prophet ﷺ was the most emotionally intelligent human being, able to read hearts, respond with compassion, and guide people according to their unique situations. In modern da‘wah—whether in our Masajid, on campuses, in interfaith settings, or online—people are not only seeking information; they are seeking connection, empathy, and authenticity. This training explores the critical role of Emotional Intelligence (EI) in da‘wah work, helping da‘ees recognize emotions (their own and others’), regulate their reactions, communicate effectively, de-escalate tension, and embody prophetic character. By the end of the session, participants will learn how EI enhances influence, builds trust, increases acceptance of the message, and avoids unnecessary conflict. EI is not a side skill—it is a prophetic tool for guidance, compassion, and wisdom.

*Session Title: “We Will Surely Cause Him to Live a Good Life”: Living the Qur’anic ‘Good Life’ in Tough Times
Description: In a world filled with uncertainty, pressure, and constant demands, the Qur’anic promise of a “good life” feels both comforting and mysterious. Allah says: “Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer—We will surely grant them a good life.”(Surah An-Nahl 16:97) But what does this “good life” actually look like?Is it material ease? Emotional stability? Barakah in time?And how can we experience it while juggling hardship, work stress, family responsibilities, and a world that seems increasingly chaotic? This session brings together two complementary voices:An Islamic scholar who will unpack the Qur’anic definition of the “good life” and the spiritual tools to attain it;A professional, father, and committed Muslim who will share how these principles come alive in the life of a modern professional balancing demanding work, family, worship, and personal struggles.Together, they will help us rediscover what it means to live a life of barakah, resilience, inner tranquility, and closeness to Allah—even in the toughest times.

Description: في زمن تتكاثر فيه الضغوط وتشتدّ المحن، يبحث الإنسان عن ملجأ داخلي يحفظ توازنه ويمنحه الطمأنينة. تأتي كلمات شيخ الإسلام ابن تيمية رحمه الله وللرجل كلمات مشهورة نقلها عنه تلميذه ابن القيم في كتابه الوابل الصيب من الكلم الطيب فيقول:سمعت شيخ الإسلام ابن تيمية قدس الله روحه يقول: "إِنَّ في الدنيا جنة من لم يدخلها لا يدخل جنة الآخرة.وقال لي مرة: ما يصنع أعدائي بي؟ أنا جنتي وبستاني في صدري، إِنَّ رُحْت فهي معي لا تفارقني، إِنَّ حبسي خلوة، وقتلي شهادة، وإخراجي من بلدي سياحة.وقال لي مرة: المحبوس من حبس قلبه عن ربه تعالى، والمأسور من أسره هواه.ولما دخل إلى السجن وصار داخل سوره نظر إليه وقال: {فضرب بينهم بسور له باب باطنه فيه الرحمة وظاهره من قبله العذاب}لتفتح لنا بابًا عظيمًا في فهم معنى الحرية الحقيقية، والكرامة الداخلية، والقوة الروحية التي لا يستطيع أحد أن ينزعها من المؤمن.هذه المحاضرة تتناول كيف يصنع الإيمان جنة داخل القلب، لا تُهزم بالسجون، ولا تُكسر بالنفي، ولا تُطفأ بالنار. سنغوص في المعاني الإيمانية التي تجعل المسلم ثابتًا أمام الابتلاء، مطمئنًا عند الاضطراب، قويًا في مواجهة الخوف والضغط، لأن مصدر سكينته ليس خارجه بل في صلته بالله.
Description_English: In a time when pressures are spreading and distressing, man is looking for an internal shelter that preserves his balance and gives him reassurance. The words of the Shikh al-Islam, the son of the Teyumah, and the man are famous words conveyed by his son of values in his hard-won book of the good words: the Shikh al-Islam, the son of the Teyuma, the saint of God, said: "Enth the delinquency of those who did not enter it shall not enter another heaven. He told me once: what makes my enemies me? I'm a fetus and a gardener in my chest, where I'm relieved she's with me. He once told me that he was locked in his heart from God. When he went to prison, he looked at him and said: " ...they will be struck by a wall with a door of mercy and its appearance of torture " to open a great door to understanding the meaning of true freedom, internal dignity and spiritual power that no one can remove from the believer. This lecture deals with how faith creates a paradise within the heart, is not defeated in prisons, is not broken in exile, and is not turned off by fire. We will dive in the faiths that make Muslims steadfast in the face of turmoil, reassured in turmoil, strong in the face of fear and pressure, because the source of his knife is not out of him, but in his connection to God.

*Session Title: Every “Musa” needs “Harun”. Together in the Struggle
Description: The story of Musa (AS) receiving Harun (AS) as support is one of the most profound Qur’anic examples of collaboration, complementarity, and unity for a divine mission. Musa (AS) did not ask for fame, ease, or assistance—he asked Allah for a partner:“And appoint for me a helper from my family — Harun, my brother.”This request teaches Muslims that no one carries a mission alone and that strength is multiplied when believers stand together.In today’s American Muslim community—diverse, multi-ethnic, and navigating rising challenges—Allah places “Haruns” in our lives: brothers and sisters from every background who complete our weaknesses, strengthen our resolve, and help us build institutions, movements, and legacies.This talk explores how cross-ethnic collaboration—African American, Arab, South Asian, Latino, and immigrant converts—forms the backbone of a resilient, influential American Muslim identity. Each speaker will guide the audience through a different angle of this prophetic model: (1) the spiritual and prophetic foundation of collaboration, (2) the practical and community-building application of collaboration across ethnic lines in America today. We rise together — or not at all.

*Session Title: Parenting Through the Pressure: Upholding Faith When Society Says Otherwise

*Session Title: Egypt & Sudan: What’s Really Happening and Why It Matters to Us
Description: Across North Africa, two nations stand at critical crossroads—Egypt and Sudan. While global headlines often overlook their struggles, the realities unfolding on the ground carry profound consequences for the region, for the global balance of power, and for the wider Ummah.This session brings together two experts delivering sequential talks, each offering a clear, accessible, and heartfelt update on the latest developments.The first speaker will unpack Egypt’s political climate, economic crisis, and shifting regional posture—explaining what is driving instability, how everyday people are affected, and how regional powers are shaping Egypt’s trajectory.The second speaker will turn to Sudan’s devastating conflict, the humanitarian catastrophe, the collapse of state institutions, and the role of international actors fueling or mitigating the crisis.Together, the talks aim to move us beyond headlines toward deeper understanding—rooted in justice, compassion, and our responsibility as part of a global Ummah. Attendees will gain insight into:What is really happening behind official narrativesHow global and regional interests shape the lives of ordinary peopleWhy the crises in Egypt and Sudan matter to American Muslims—morally, politically, and strategicallyConcrete ways to stay informed, support relief, and advocate effectivelyThis session is both an update and a call to conscience—inviting us to recognize the suffering, resilience, and dignity of our brothers and sisters, and to reaffirm our responsibility toward an Ummah bound together by faith and shared destiny.

Do not grieve over them; do not be distressed by their scheming, (16:127) How can we take care of our mental health while also working towards our future? On the other hand, how can we focus on our futures without becoming numb or complacent while witnessing these atrocities?

*Session Title: The Test of Comfort: Staying Faithful in Times of Ease
Description: Hardship often awakens faith, pushes the believer to call upon Allah, and sharpens one’s sense of purpose. But comfort, ease, and privilege carry a different kind of test—one far more subtle and often far more dangerous. Allah reminds us:“But as for he who fears standing before his Lord and restrains his desires—Paradise will be his refuge.” (An-Nāziʿāt 79:40–41) This session explores a critical but neglected reality: not all believers are tested through oppression or adversity—some are tested through comfort, distraction, and abundance. While trials of hardship expose our patience, trials of ease expose our sincerity. Comfort can dull the heart, weaken resolve, and make us forget our purpose unless we remain alert, grateful, and disciplined. Through Qur’anic guidance, prophetic teachings, and lived examples, the speakers will highlight how times of ease demand vigilance, introspection, and intentional effort to stay close to Allah. The audience will walk away understanding the unseen dangers of comfort, practical ways to maintain spiritual discipline, and how to transform privilege into a means of servitude, gratitude, and purpose.

*Session Title: "It's Okay To Not Be Okay"

*Session Title: Between Ideals and Pragmatism: Turkey’s Regional Actions in Gaza, Libya, and Syria and the Transformation at Home
Description: In a region defined by shifting alliances, persistent conflicts, and evolving public expectations, Turkey stands as one of the most influential—and scrutinized—actors. In this session, a member of the Turkish Parliament offers an insider’s perspective on how Turkey navigates the delicate balance between moral principles and political pragmatism across multiple fronts.The talk will explore Turkey’s current role in Gaza, including government policies, diplomatic efforts, and the unprecedented grassroots mobilization of the Turkish public. It will also examine Turkey’s strategic presence in Libya and Syria, highlighting how humanitarian commitments, geopolitical calculations, and security concerns intersect on the ground.Finally, the session turns inward, addressing the transformations within Turkey’s own political landscape: How is public support for the AK Party changing? What internal and external dynamics are shaping the country’s political future? And what does this mean for Turkey’s long-term regional stance?This talk offers a rare opportunity to hear directly from a policymaker deeply involved in Turkey’s regional and domestic affairs—providing clarity, context, and honest reflection on one of the Muslim world’s most pivotal players.
Speakers: Işık Ercan; Meryem Göka; Rümeysa Kadak

*Session Title: Empowering Muslim American Communities in End-of-Life Medical Decision-Making: Faith, Autonomy, and Education
Description: This presentation examines end‑of‑life medical decision‑making in Muslim American communities through a mosque‑based, multilingual qualitative study. Findings demonstrate how faith, family roles, communication barriers, and legal frameworks shape disclosure practices and contribute to low use of advance directives, highlighting misalignment between patient wishes and documented directives. These insights are guiding community education and healthcare provider training to advance culturally responsive models of care.

*Session Title: Lowering the Gaze

Drawing on Qur’anic examples, prophetic teachings, and real-life family dynamics, our speakers will guide parents toward building a home environment where sibling relationships are strengthened through compassion, teamwork, and shared identity. Because while parents may not always be there to guide every step, a child who has a loving sister or brother has a lifelong ally.

*Session Title: Panel Discussion: My Ummah and American Influence
Description: America plays a powerful and complex role in shaping global events that impact the Muslim Ummah—from foreign policy and military alliances to humanitarian aid, media narratives, and cultural norms. For Muslims at home and abroad, the United States can be both a source of harm and a force for positive influence. As Gaza, Sudan, and other crises unfold, the question becomes: How does American influence shape the destiny of the Ummah—and what is our responsibility within that system?This panel brings together three expert voices—a policy-making professional, a sociologist/community organizer, and a Turkish parliament member—to explore how American political decisions, social movements, and transnational relationships shape the wellbeing of Muslim communities worldwide. Through an open, dialog-style conversation, panelists will examine U.S. foreign policy, grassroots influence, diaspora activism, and shifting global alliances, while discussing how Muslims can strategically use their position within America to uplift the Ummah.This is not merely a critique of American power—it is an honest, holistic exploration of how Muslims can understand, navigate, and harness influence within the world’s most powerful nation to advocate for justice, protect vulnerable populations, and strengthen the bonds of the global Ummah.

*Session Title: Stay Here or Go Elsewhere?
Description: Over the past two years, countless Muslims—especially younger generations—have expressed deep frustration, moral fatigue, and disillusionment with living in a country whose government has been complicit in the genocide of Palestinians. Statements like “I can’t keep paying taxes to a government doing this,” “I don’t see a future here,” and “Maybe I should just leave” have become increasingly common.This is not a question with a single correct answer, nor a matter of religious obligation to remain or to migrate. Rather, it is a deeply personal, deeply emotional, and deeply strategic question that deserves mature, nuanced discussion. This session aims to address that conversation head-on.The session will explore the internal struggle many Muslims are facing: (a) We will unpack the emotional, ethical, and spiritual dimensions of the dilemma—acknowledging the pain, the disillusionment, and the legitimacy of the concerns. (b) We will expand on the strategic, community-centered, and forward-looking perspective—what it means to build, influence, and create positive change here, while understanding that no place on earth offers a perfect, utopian existence.This session does not tell people what choice to make. Instead, it gives them the clarity, frameworks, and grounded Islamic principles to evaluate their own circumstances and make decisions with confidence and responsibility.At its heart, the discussion encourages Muslims to view their presence—wherever they choose to be—not merely as residents, but as agents of change, with a mission, a voice, and the potential to shape the future.

*Session Title: "We will strengthen your arm through your brother..."
Description: In the Qur’an, Allah reassures Musa (AS): “We will strengthen your arm through your brother.” This divine wisdom teaches us that in moments of hardship, the believer is never meant to stand alone. Today, our Ummah is wounded—Gaza under brutal siege, Sudan suffering unimaginable devastation, and families in our own neighborhoods torn apart by ICE detentions. In these times of fear, grief, and uncertainty, our strength must come from one another.This talk explores how Muslims in America can embody this Qur’anic principle by building bonds of solidarity, compassion, and courageous action. It highlights our duty to stand with the oppressed, support affected families, strengthen our masajid, and remain connected as a community. When the world collapses around us, we—like Musa and Harun—must rise together, because in unity, Allah places barakah, strength, and victory.

When Support Isn’t Support: The Hidden Motives Behind Right-Wing Anti-Zionism
Description: In recent months, a growing wave of “anti-Zionist” rhetoric has emerged from segments of the right wing. At face value, this seems like a surprising development—voices that once championed unconditional support for Israel are now criticizing Zionism. But beneath the surface lies a deeper, more troubling reality: much of this rhetoric is not driven by moral clarity, compassion for Palestinians, or a genuine commitment to justice. Instead, it is rooted in white supremacist ideology, xenophobia, replacement theories, and anti-immigrant hostility.This session warns Muslims against assuming that every voice opposing Zionism is a trustworthy or principled ally. We will unpack this issue from two angles: (a) we will trace the rise of right-wing “anti-Zionist” narratives and expose the ideological foundations that drive them. (b) We will focus on Muslim responsibility—how to navigate alliances wisely, avoid being weaponized, and remain anchored in Islamic ethics and justice-based activism.

*Session Title: Campus Activism: The True Meaning of Jihad
Description: Oftentimes, our campuses feel like a battleground. College is no longer just filled with homework or social struggles. Our students have now taken the role of fighting for justice on campus. While some of these efforts may have started small, we have seen an inundation of students ready to answer the call to stand for justice within their universities. But where is Islam in this movement? Throughout our efforts, we may forget to keep Allah SWT at the center of our cause. What does it mean to truly fight for something for the sake of Allah SWT? Allah SWT tells us in Surah Al-Ankabut , وَٱلَّذِينَ جَـٰهَدُوا۟ فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَمَعَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ But We shall be sure to guide to Our ways those who strive hard for Our cause: God is with those who do good (29:29). How can we strive for the cause of Allah SWT on campus? How do we sacrifice our comfortability in a way that is impactful and beneficial? Most importantly, what does jihad mean in our modern times and how can we achieve it within our capacities?

*Session Title: When Roles Reverse:  Caring For Our Parents As They Age
Description: No matter what we do, we can never repay our parents for the sacrifices they made—Allah ﷻ reminds us that gratitude to Him is tied to gratitude to them. Yet as they grow older, many of us struggle with complex emotions: guilt when we can’t do enough, frustration when their needs feel overwhelming, or even anger when their aging changes the relationship we once knew. We’ll explore practical ways to care for them with dignity and patience, address common pitfalls to avoid, and learn how to transform this stage of life into a means of barakah and immense reward.

*Session Title: From Mecca to Al Madinah: Thriving as Muslims in America Beyond Survival
Description: This session draws on one of the most powerful historical arcs in Islam—the journey from Mecca to Madinah—to help American Muslims understand where we stand today and where we must go next.The 13 years in Mecca were defined by pressure, hardship, survival, and spiritual fortification. Yet those very years laid the foundation for the next 10 years in Madinah—an era of institution-building, community growth, social reform, and global leadership.In the same way, American Muslims are navigating a period of intense challenges—Islamophobia, political pressure, cultural confusion, economic instability, and identity struggles. But these struggles are not signs of weakness; they are the crucibles that shape a community capable of thriving.This session features two speakers—each covering a distinct stage of the “Mecca–Madinah model”—to guide the community through a clear vision:We must first survive with faith and resilience, then build with strategy and purpose.Focus includes: strengthening Muslim institutions, economic empowerment, political power, and shaping the long-term future of Islam in America.

Description: This session will explore the evolving landscape of public opinion in the United States regarding the Palestinian cause. It will examine shifts in the general American mood, as well as within the Democratic and Republican parties, against the backdrop of Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza and U.S. complicity. A central question will be whether these transformations are enduring or temporary, and how advocates can strategically engage with them to advance justice and policy change.This session will provide a descriptive and analytical framework for understanding these transformations and their diverse expressions. Identify the challenges and opportunities that accompany these shifts. Explore strategies to sustain, expand, and deepen momentum, moving from changes in public, partisan, and generational attitudes into the realm of policymaking. Examine counter-strategies employed by pro-Israel actors to suppress or reverse these transformations. Analyze how Islamophobia and xenophobia are weaponized to divert attention from genocide in Gaza and U.S. complicity. Assess the influence of the Zionist lobby and its allies in state institutions, particularly in suppressing freedom of expression and academic freedoms related to Palestine, and discuss effective methods of resistance.

Description: في زمنٍ كثرت فيه الأزمات واضطربت فيه القيم، يبرز سؤالٌ جوهري: ما قيمة وجودنا في حياة الناس؟ هل نحن مجرّد عابرين في هذه الدنيا، أم رسلُ رحمةٍ وخيرٍ حيثما حللنا؟يحدّثنا القرآن على لسان عيسى عليه السلام بقوله: ﴿وَجَعَلَنِي مُبَارَكًا أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُ﴾ آيةٌ قصيرة في كلماتها، عميقة في معناها، ترسم ملامح الإنسان الذي لا يُقاس بقوّته ولا بشهرته، بل بأثره.وصفٌ بليغٌ قاله النبي ﷺ: “مثل المؤمن كمثل الغيث، أينما وقع نفع.” فالمؤمن الحقيقي ليس من يملأ المكان ضجيجًا، بل من يملأه خيرًا، وأمانًا، وطمأنينة، وبصيرة.هذه المحاضرة ليست عن المثاليات، بل عن كيف يصبح كل واحدٍ منّا مصدر بركة؟ في بيته، في عمله، في مجتمعه، في موقفه من الحق، وفي طريقه إلى الله.

This lecture isn't about ideals, it's about how each of us becomes a pool source? In his home, in his work, in his community, in his position on the right, on his way to God.

Panel DIscussion Proactive and Reactive Responses to ICE
Description: Recent increases in ICE activity have resurfaced fear and anxiety within Muslim and immigrant communities across the country. Families are worried, Masājid are uncertain about their responsibilities, and many individuals feel unprepared for encounters with law enforcement. This panel brings together a community organizer, an immigration lawyer, and an advocate who directly represents detained immigrants to provide a holistic, grounded response to this moment. Together, they will address both proactive and reactive measures—equipping attendees with critical knowledge, legal tools, community strategies, and faith-based guidance. Instead of reacting through fear or misinformation, this session will empower participants to move with clarity, preparation, and unity. Attendees will gain practical steps for protecting themselves, their families, and their institutions, while understanding the Islamic principles that anchor us during periods of pressure, injustice, and uncertainty.This is not just a conversation about danger—it is a roadmap toward resilience, advocacy, and collective strength.

*Session Title: “And being dutiful to parents…”
Description: For many of us, college is our first time away from our families. Whether we live away from home for school, or spend countless hours on campus for extracurriculars and studying, our time with family is sometimes nonexistent. There is oftentimes a guilt associated with spending less time with family in exchange for pursuing a career. Allah SWT tells us in Surah Al-Isra, ۞ وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَـٰنًا ۚ إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفٍّۢ وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوْلًۭا كَرِيمًۭا Your Lord has commanded that you should worship none but Him, and that you be kind to your parents. If either or both of them reach old age with you, say no word that shows impatience with them, and do not be harsh with them, but speak to them respectfully (17:23). What does Islam tell us about our duties to our family? How can we balance both our responsibilities to our parents and to our futures? On the other hand, how do I balance my newfound independence with obeying my parents and their wishes?

*Session Title: This Too Shall Pass
Description: One of the most humbling quotes of all time. It is the perfect reminder that this life, this dunya is not the end game. Although we experience a wide spectrum of life's up and downs that we are working towards our akhira. When you sit down at the end of an amazing day and think to yourself well this might just be one of the best days of my life remember that this too shall pass that no matter how good these times feel, that it won't last forever. The top of the rollercoaster is only at the top for so long before it comes down. *Session Title: Anchored by Faith: Together, We Rise
Description: In moments of global turmoil, social fragmentation, and personal uncertainty, believers are not meant to merely endure the storm—they are meant to rise through it. Our strength comes from being anchored in divine truth and guided by Allah, whose wisdom and justice extend far beyond the chaos around us. This talk explores how Muslims can move from survival mode to a state of spiritual strength, communal resilience, and moral clarity.When fear spreads, faith becomes our anchor. When confusion dominates, revelation becomes our compass. And when the world fractures, unity becomes our power. Now is the time for the Ummah to stand together—faithful in heart, focused in mission, and fearless in conviction—so we can rise collectively, respond courageously, and be agents of light in an age overwhelmed by darkness.
